text:
kai_acme: Hey team — running into a weird one. Our client started getting 400s from /v1/embeddings: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" after we switched to gzipped ndjson batching. Happening for ~350 items in one payload. Any ideas?

emma_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request headers + a small example payload (sanitized)? Also any request_id from the 400 response?

kai_acme: request_id=rn-9a2b3c, headers: Content-Type: application/x-ndjson, Content-Encoding: gzip, Accept: application/json. We gzipped the ndjson on client side. Minimal payload (uncompressed) I think looked like:

{"input": "[0.12,0.34,0.56,...]"}
{"input": "[0.01,0.02,0.03,...]"}

We realized the inner arrays are stringified because our serializer calls json.dumps on numpy arrays before writing lines. Might that cause the server to treat the whole string as a single text input and attempt to embed it as text (hence 1536 output) vs we thought we'd be upserting already-computed vectors (1024)?

emma_support: That matches what we see in the logs for rn-9a2b3c — server treated each line as text. Our embeddings model returns 1536 dims by default for text inputs; 1024 dims was for the older custom model you were using earlier. Two things to check: 1) are you trying to call /embeddings to submit precomputed vectors (we don't accept raw vectors on that endpoint), 2) confirm you didn't double-stringify the arrays.

lina_engineer: Quick note: if your client is sending strings like "[0.1,0.2]" in the JSON that's still a single text field. The embeddings API will tokenize that string and produce an embedding of the tokens. Also Content-Encoding: gzip + application/x-ndjson is fine, but the line format must be valid JSON objects where fields are proper types (arrays should be arrays, not stringified arrays).

kai_acme: Ahhh ok. We actually pre-compute vectors on-device and were trying to store them via embeddings endpoint (old workflow). We misremembered. So what is the recommended path if we want to store our own vectors?

emma_support: Two options: 1) If you want to store precomputed vectors in your DB/ops, send them to your vector DB directly (don't use embeddings endpoint). 2) If you need Redwood to accept raw vectors for downstream features, we have a dedicated ingest API (private) — open a ticket for enterprise ingest support. For now, to get consistent dims from us, send the original raw text as arrays of strings and let the embeddings model compute vectors.

raj_sre: Also watch for mixed-type batches. We saw one payload where some lines were proper JSON with "input": ["a string"], and some lines were "input": "[0.1,0.2]" (string). That causes the model selection and dimension expectations to vary, producing intermittent 400s. Keep batch type consistent.

kai_acme: Understood. We're going to fix the client to never json.dumps numpy arrays before writing lines. Quick question — we were gzipping because of throughput limits. Any gotchas with gzip + ndjson you can share?

lina_engineer: Gzip is fine. Two gotchas: 1) set Content-Encoding: gzip (you did), 2) ensure each newline-delimited line is a valid JSON object after decompression. Example correct uncompressed NDJSON: 

{"input": "This is a doc to embed"}
{"input": "Another doc"}

If you want to batch multiple texts per request, pass input as an array: 

{"input": ["doc1","doc2","doc3"]}

For vector-like data (numbers) you must not send to embeddings endpoint as precomputed vectors — that's why you're getting mismatched dims.

emma_support: Also, if you must send arrays (e.g., array of strings per line), confirm the JSON encoder doesn't collapse types: use native lists, not stringified lists. For python+numpy a safe pattern: 

# bad
line = {"input": json.dumps(np_array.tolist())}  # produces a string
# good
line = {"input": np_array.tolist()}  # produces a list

kai_acme: Fix deployed to staging. Replayed the same gzipped NDJSON with proper lists and now we get 200s and vectors length 1536 consistently. Thanks! :raised_hands:

ingest-bot: Note: escalated ticket #INC-4321 marked resolved by support (cause: client-side stringified arrays).

emma_support: Glad to hear. For follow-ups we can add a quick note in our SDK docs about common numpy pitfalls. Filing a small doc PR. :memo:
